sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Lesson 8.7, Kaito! Today we tackle workflow reproducibility. In machine learning, training runs often fail to reproduce because pipelines rely on manual bash scripts or untracked notebooks.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Exactly! If someone changes an evaluation metric or tunes a single hyperparameter, re-running a monolithic script forces you to recompute heavy raw data ingestion from scratch, which takes hours!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely. By formalizing computational pipelines as content-addressed DAGs, Data Version Control executes only stages whose input hashes have mutated, restoring unchanged stages from cache in zero time.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So instead of writing run_all.sh that executes every script sequentially, we define each stage in dvc.yaml with explicit dependencies and outputs?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exactly. In a shell script, the machine has no awareness of data lineage. If stage two outputs are already valid on disk, bash still blindly runs stage two. DVC inspects the graph to see what actually needs computing.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: And that means if I only tweak an evaluation parameter, stages one, two, and three don't execute at all!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Wait Dr. Nova, why do we need to hash the command line string cmd(s) along with code and data? Isn't the code hash enough?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Great question, Kaito! Suppose train.py accepts command-line arguments like --epochs 10 versus --epochs 100. The source file train.py has identical hash C(s), but cmd(s) completely changes the training execution and the resulting weights.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Ah! So hashing the full tuple: command, code, params, and data dependencies guarantees true execution immutability!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So if B(s) is True, DVC doesn't execute Python at all? What actually happens to the output files on disk?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: On modern file systems like APFS, Btrfs, or XFS, DVC creates copy-on-write reflinks or hardlinks from .dvc/cache into your workspace. Restoring a 50-gigabyte parquet dataset takes less than 50 milliseconds!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Fifty milliseconds for 50 gigabytes! That explains why DVC pipelines feel instantaneous on unchanged stages.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So Amdahl's Law proves that the more time we invest in heavy upstream data cleaning, the greater our speedup when tuning downstream models!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely. Consider an autonomous vehicle vision team: frame extraction and undistortion take 216 minutes out of a 240-minute cold run. That is a 90% cached fraction.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Which gives a 10x speedup! In an eight-hour workday, an engineer can run 11 experimental iterations instead of just 2. That is a five-and-a-half-fold surge in team velocity!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the DAG simulator docked below us! I'm clicking Tune Hyperparams right now. Wow, look at the canvas! Ingest and Features stayed green with checkmarks, and only Train and Eval re-ran in 75 seconds!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exactly, Kaito. Because params.yaml was only consumed by Train and Eval, the stage fingerprints for Ingest and Features remained identical in dvc.lock. Now try clicking Ingest New Raw Data.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Whoa! Every single node turned amber and executed from scratch for the full 240 seconds! That illustrates upstream dependency cascades perfectly!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! If an engineer only adds a Python comment, the compiler ignores it, but what does SHA-256 do to the raw file bitstream?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Remember Definition 8.7.1, Kaito: SHA-256 evaluates raw file bits. Look closely at Option A: does DVC re-execute Stage 2, and what tool normalizes code AST before hashing?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So if my pipeline has three feature extraction branches that take 10 minutes, 20 minutes, and 60 minutes, throwing 100 CPU cores at it won't finish in 10 minutes?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Correct, Kaito! The 60-minute branch is on the critical path. Even if the 10-minute and 20-minute branches finish almost instantly, the terminal stage cannot begin until the 60-minute dependency completes.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: That's why optimizing the critical path yields massive speedups, while optimizing non-critical branches has zero effect on total makespan!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Looking at this comparison, the pipeline's architecture directly dictates our iteration speed! If we put fast-changing hyperparameters in stage one, we'd destroy our caching!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely. Production ML architecture follows the principle of stage invariance: place heavy, immutable data transformations as far upstream as possible, and isolate volatile hyperparameters to terminal stages.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: That way, 90% of our pipeline stays frozen in cache, and our experimentation loop stays lightning fast!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the cost curves in Simulator Tab B! The red line shows naive re-execution exploding to 14,400 dollars in a single month at 32 dollars an hour!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Indeed, Kaito. By caching 68.8% of stage computation, the teal curve stays flat at 4,500 dollars. That is 9,900 dollars saved every month, or nearly 120,000 dollars annually for a single pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: And the engineers get a 3.2x speedup on every single pull request test run! It's both cheaper and faster!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2! In Case 1, Training and Evaluation execute, which is 300 plus 20 seconds, saving 210 seconds. In Case 2, Ingestion mutates, which cascades all the way to the end!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on, Kaito. Check the options carefully: Option B matches our exact derivation of 320 seconds for Case 1 and 530 seconds full rerun for Case 2.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Planet Labs saving 450,000 dollars a year just by caching atmospheric calibration stages is incredible! That proves data versioning directly impacts cloud operational budgets.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: And notice Nuro's CI/CD gate: by requiring dvc repro and dvc metrics diff in pull requests, unversioned weights or regression-prone models cannot physically deploy to delivery vehicles on public streets.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So DVC isn't just about speed—it provides safety governance for production machine learning systems!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Final Capstone Checkpoint! In Part 1, 90% cached gives a 10x speedup, jumping workday iterations from 2 runs to 11 runs—a 5.5x net throughput surge!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: And in Part 2, Path 2 from A to C to E totals 10 plus 60 plus 25, which is 95 minutes. Comparing sequential 175 minutes against 95 minutes yields a 1.842x parallel speedup. Select Option A on the card below!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: I've seen engineers put datetime.now() inside their pipeline config, and then wonder why DVC refuses to cache anything!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: A classic trap, Kaito. Because params.yaml changes every second, Definition 8.7.1 mutates the stage key on every invocation, defeating memoization entirely.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: And configuring cache.type to reflink or hardlink prevents duplicating gigabytes of data while protecting OS inodes!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: This Python engine captures the exact semantics of DVC! The recursive compute_stage_key resolves ancestor digests cleanly, ensuring any upstream change cascades.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Indeed, Kaito. And run_repro implements the Memoization Bypass Predicate: whenever a key is present in stage_cache, it increments bypassed and adds zero runtime.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: What an enlightening session on DVC pipelines, Dr. Nova! By replacing fragile bash scripts with declarative DAGs, our machine learning workflows gain the same rigorous reproducibility as compiled software!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Indeed, Kaito. By mastering content-addressed stage keys, memoization bypass, and Amdahl's Law, you protect engineering velocity and prevent production model regressions. Join us next in Lesson 8.8 for Best Practices!
